nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Year-round strong light drives growth in the canopy, while little of it reaches the forest floor.

nodes.name: Heavy rainfall
nodes.desc: Wet-season rain keeps the lowland rainforest, swamps and rivers of the Darien green and flooded.

nodes.name: Tides and river flooding
nodes.desc: Coastal tides and flooding rivers soak the swamps and mangroves along the Pacific side of the site.

nodes.name: Forest soil and leaf litter
nodes.desc: Fallen leaves, fruit and dung build a litter layer that returns nutrients to the roots of forest plants.

nodes.name: Fungi and bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead leaves, wood and animals in the warm, wet litter, returning nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Fig trees
nodes.desc: Figs fruit through much of the year and are a favoured food of howler monkeys and many fruit-eating birds and bats.

nodes.name: Trumpet trees
nodes.desc: Fast-growing pioneer trees of forest gaps and clearings; their leaves and fruit feed sloths and many other animals.

nodes.name: Red mangrove
nodes.desc: Stilt-rooted trees that line the tidal coast and shelter the shore, with leaves that some reptiles eat.

nodes.name: Mantled howler
nodes.desc: A leaf-eating monkey that also takes fruit, especially figs, and helps spread and germinate seeds.

nodes.name: Brown-throated sloth
nodes.desc: A slow tree-dweller that feeds on leaves of forest trees such as Cecropia, and is the main prey of harpy eagles.

nodes.name: Baird's tapir
nodes.desc: A large forest browser eating leaves, shoots and fruit, often at treefalls; only jaguars and large crocodiles can take adults.

nodes.name: Collared peccary
nodes.desc: Piglike herd animal that eats fruit, seeds, roots and some small animals; jaguars and cougars hunt it.

nodes.name: Jamaican fruit bat
nodes.desc: The most-recorded mammal near the site; it feeds on fruit such as figs and carries seeds through the forest at night.

nodes.name: Green iguana
nodes.desc: A large leaf- and fruit-eating lizard of the canopy and riverbanks, itself prey for many birds, snakes and cats.

nodes.name: Keel-billed toucan
nodes.desc: A big-billed bird that eats mainly fruit, including figs, and so spreads seeds across the forest.

nodes.name: Tome's spiny rat
nodes.desc: A common forest rodent that eats seeds and fruit on the ground and is food for snakes, hawks and small cats.

nodes.name: Roadside hawk
nodes.desc: A common medium-sized raptor of forest edges that hunts lizards, small mammals and large insects.

nodes.name: Terciopelo
nodes.desc: A large pit viper of lowland forest that ambushes rodents, lizards and frogs.

nodes.name: Ocelot
nodes.desc: A medium-sized spotted cat that hunts rodents, lizards and other small animals on the forest floor.

nodes.name: Black vulture
nodes.desc: The most-recorded bird near the site; it recycles carrion and is recorded feeding on dead iguanas.

nodes.name: Jaguar
nodes.desc: The largest cat of the Americas, taking peccaries, tapirs, sloths and other large prey; near-threatened.

nodes.name: Harpy eagle
nodes.desc: A huge forest eagle that takes mostly sloths and monkeys from the canopy; the site holds an important population.

nodes.name: Cougar
nodes.desc: A wide-ranging cat that hunts peccaries and other mid-sized mammals, sharing the forest with the jaguar.
